summary: Big Ledge light at Cockerwit Passage, Shelburne County: lit 1900 with keeper James E. Goodwin to 1930; rebuilt in the 1960s; closed, best seen from shore.

structures.note: Square wooden building with sloping sides, painted white, under an octagonal iron lantern; 28 ft from pier to vane (report, cite 1). NSLPS: no longer standing.
White square tower with red top. Built 1962 to 1965 (NSLPS); about 1963 (Lighthouse Friends).

access.note: Grounds and tower closed; site reached by boat.

visit.note: Light visible from the shore at Lower Woods Harbour, about 800 m from the wharf.

events.note: Put in operation 1 September 1900 (Department of Marine and Fisheries).
Built by days' labour under Amos McLellan at a cost of $1,478.10.
Hand fog horn at the station, sounded in answer to signals from vessels.
Fog horn installed at the light (NSLPS).
Original tower replaced between 1962 and 1965 (NSLPS); present tower built about 1963 (Lighthouse Friends).

keepers.name: James E. Goodwin
keepers.note: Spelled Jas. E. Goodwin in the Department tables. Lighthouse Friends gives appointment on 27 August 1900 and service to April 1930, with salary rising from $200 to $966. The 1910 table (cite 2) lists Woods Harbour with Jas. E. Goodwin at $265; the 1915 table (cite 3) gives Goodwin with appointment 27 Aug. 1900. Both table reads are by column position in the OCR.

keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends only. No Department table for his years was read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Four sources give four descriptions: the Coast Guard list (LFl W 6s, flash 2 s, eclipse 4 s), Lighthouse Friends (one-second flash, five-second eclipse), NSLPS (Fixed White, 1992) and OSM (Fl W 6s). We used the Coast Guard list as the current official entry. The other three are not reconciled and are listed for the editor.

notes_for_editor: Facts: first lighting (1900), the 1900 build and its cost, the first keeper's appointment date and the 1963 rebuild are the best supported. (1) Position-read tables, now checked against the page images (2026-10-28): the 1910 salary row is on printed p. 258 (scan 260) and reads 'Woods Harbour / Jas. E. Goodwin / Aug. 27, 1900 / 265 00', confirmed. The 1915 keepers' table is on scan 79 (printed p. 72) and reads '*Woods harbour / J. Goodwin / Aug. 27, 1900 / 345 00', confirmed; the OCR had misread the initial as 'T.' and the salary row reads 'Woods harbour' in the image. (2) Chetwynd (1930 to 1953) rests on Lighthouse Friends alone; no Department table for those years was read. (3) Characteristic conflicts are in resolved_conflicts. NSLPS also calls a later tower 'Woods Harbour II' and marks it decommissioned, while the Coast Guard list gives the present light as active; the story follows the Coast Guard. (4) NSLPS gives the lens change as 1990 to 1992 and the fog horn as 1960 and 1962; these are not checked beyond NSLPS and are not used in the story except the fog horn in the 1962 event. (5) No wreck, storm or rescue was found in the sources read; the wrecks list is empty and the story has no storm chapter. (6) The 1900 report prints the cost as '$1,478,10' (checked on scan 63, printed p. 48); the story gives $1,478.10 and says the report prints a comma. (7) Nothing in the record was changed; the county field is null in the record and the 1900 report names Shelburne County. (8) Fact-check edits (2026-10-28): 6.3 m replacement now cited to Lighthouse Friends and CCG (not the 1900 report); 'expected' replaced by the report's 'should be visible'; 'by 1993' replaces '1993 or earlier'; the 'no other source names him' and 'ledge is closed' sentences were removed; NSLPS access wording is 'by boat'.
